case_name: Smt. Mira Mondal (Nee Biswas) v. Shri Jyotirmoy Mondal
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1973 and had two daughters. The relationship deteriorated over time due to arrogance, misunderstanding, lack of feelings for each other, and continuous ill-treatment. The respondent/husband instituted a Mat Suit No.51 of 1997 against the appellant/wife for dissolution of the marriage by a decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: Evidence of a child witness indicating cruelty of the mother towards the children cannot have any bearing on the allegation of cruelty of the wife against the husband.
legal_principles.held: This court holds that evidence of a child witness indicating cruelty of the mother towards the children cannot have any bearing on the allegation of cruelty of the wife against the husband.
cited_cases: Smti Ananta V. Ramchander, (2009) AIR Cal 167

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must establish that the other party has been guilty of cruelty.
legal_principles.held: The law is clear that a party seeking divorce must establish that the other party has been guilty of cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision to grant divorce was upheld, and the appeal was dismissed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for dissolution of marriage
